owner_and_source: Cordeau & Laporte dial-a-ride benchmark instances (type-a set, a2-16..a8-96). Origin: J.-F. Cordeau (2006), 'A Branch-and-Cut Algorithm for the Dial-a-Ride Problem', Operations Research 54(3):573-586; instances distributed via HEC Montreal (neumann.hec.ca/chairedistributique/data/). Acquired from the widely-used public mirror github.com/davidrey123/DARP (Instances/Cordeau.zip).
license_and_commercial_rights: Academic benchmark instances, published for open forge/research/benchmarking use; no formal software license is attached to the instance files themselves, and none is claimed here. The instances contain only synthetic coordinates/time-windows (no proprietary or personal data). Used here strictly for algorithm benchmarking/comparison against published best-known values, the standard and unrestricted research use for this dataset. Not resold or redistributed as a product; commercial benchmarking/comparison of a solver against them is the established norm in the field.
schema_and_format: Zip archive of 24 plain-text Cordeau-format DARP instances (Cordeau/aK-N.txt). Each file: header line 'K n T Q L' (K vehicles, n requests, T max route duration, Q vehicle capacity, L max ride time), then 2n+2 node lines 'id x y service_duration load earliest latest' -- node 0 and 2n+1 are the depot, nodes 1..n are pickups (load +q), nodes n+1..2n are the paired drop-offs (load -q). Travel time between nodes equals Euclidean distance; the objective is total routing distance.
update_frequency: static (a fixed, decades-stable academic benchmark set)
canonical_contract: metis.decide.darp_ir.DarpInstance (parsed by metis.decide.darp_loader); benchmarked by aletheia/benchmarks/quality/darp_benchmark.py against published best-known/optimal values

quality_tests.name: valid_zip
quality_tests.description: retained object is a non-empty zip archive

quality_tests.name: parses_to_instances
quality_tests.description: each member parses to a DarpInstance whose node count equals 2n+2 and whose header K/n/T/Q/L are all positive

acceptance_threshold: downloads, sha256 matches the recorded checksum, is a readable zip containing 24 Cordeau-format instance files that parse cleanly
retention_and_deletion: retain as part of the solver-quality benchmark corpus; cheaply reproducible (re-fetchable from the upstream mirror) so evictable first
